messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: O3 for stanc.exe
parts:
On Fri, Oct 12, 2012 at 8:48 AM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
> On Friday, October 12, 2012 11:26:54 AM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
>>
> Very tangentially related. Is it possible in the makefiles to just ignore
> the optimization level for the bin/stanc{.exe} target only? Am I correct in
> thinking that using -O3 is essentially useless for the parser and just takes
> more time and RAM to compile? The only thing that makes me concerned is that
> make bin/stanc also compiles libstan where I guess that O3 is important.

In Windows, we need O3. If the executable gets any larger, g++
crashes. That means that stanc.exe can't compile under O2, O1, or O0
under windows at this time. Bob has been refactoring it periodically,
but we're pretty much at the limit of what g++ 4.6.3 under Windows can
do in terms of size.


Daniel
